page.layout: One page of text: a centred heading "AD LECTOREM." above a body of running text in italic with a large woodcut initial P at the left; no margin notes. Below the text, at the lower right, a catchword "PHI-".

p.i: Aruulam habes Philoso-phiam, Bone Lector, sed fortasse non respuendam. Scis enim, illud esse, tam naturæ, quàm artis ingenium, vt quidquid melius est, in exiguis con-dat. Certè nostra tenuitas nil habet exactius, quod in vno vix lapsi anni decursu elaborauerit. Sed qualecumque hoc sit, vel me reclamante, in publicum exit. Sic prorsus licuit Dilectissimo inter discipulos D. MARCO BEMBO. Hic Adolescens, ingenio, & studio maximus operarum à se conscriptam in vulgus mittit. Prius tamen cum eo pacisceba, vt libelltherefore inscriberet epigraphe: Ad vsum studiosæ Iuuentutis. Inde intelligis, destinari ad Philosophiam nouitios quod non sine rubore in manus iret Sapientum. Sin vero & ad hos casu venerit, nil magis habebit in votis, quàm vt corrigatur. Sic ego morem Apelli geram: Quidquid ceteri arguerint, audiam sub tabula, & meliorem veritatis colorem Philosophiæ reponam.

page.notes: The woodcut initial P is joined to the first word. Some words in the text are printed in a damaged or blurred state; the line "Prius tamen cum eo pacisceba, vt libel-lo inscriberet" reads as printed but the word "therefore" in that line is a misreading and should be "lo"; this is marked for checking: pacisceba [?]. The word "operarum" is a doubtful reading of "opera". The catchword PHI- is at the lower right.
